def greedy_path(env, Q, max_steps=200):
    """Follow argmax_a Q(s, a) from the start state through the deterministic dynamics.

    env : Env

    s = np.flatnonzero(env.start).item()

title: Temporal-Difference Learning
text:
Cliff Walking
The point of the cliff is that the optimal path and the safe path differ. The shortest route runs along the very edge of the cliff. Notice though, that with \(\varepsilon=0.1\) that route also means a one-in-ten chance per step of being blown into the cliff for \(-100\) reward.

Q-learning learns the values of the optimal path and falls into the cliff regularly. Its online return is the worst of the three learners even though its \(Q\) is the most correct.
Sarsa learns the values of its own \(\varepsilon\)-greedy behavior, which include the cliff risk, so it backs off to a safer route and earns more per episode.

That is the on-policy/off-policy distinction paying a visible dividend, in both directions.

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
Utilities & Environment Setup
A hands-on companion to Chapter 7 of Sutton & Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction.
In the previous chapter we learned about methods that bootstrap off of a one-step lookahead of the next state, and prior to that we looked at Monte Carlo methods that didn’t bootstrap at all, hence, needing to wait until the end of an episode to learn anything. In this chapter, we look at methods that are intermediary between those two extremes.
Specifically, we look \(n\) steps ahead and bootstrap off the state you find there:
\[
G_{t:t+n} \doteq R_{t+1} + \gamma R_{t+2} + \cdots + \gamma^{n-1}R_{t+n} + \gamma^{n}V_{t+n-1}(S_{t+n})
\]
Notice that when \(n = 1\), we get back TD(0), and when \(n \ge T-t\) we get back the Monte Carlo return.
Everything in between is what we will be working through in this chapter.
As with everything, there is no free-lunch. The \(n\)-step return is not available until time \(t+n\), so the update
\[
V_{t+n}(S_t) \doteq V_{t+n-1}(S_t) + \alpha\left[G_{t:t+n} - V_{t+n-1}(S_t)\right]
\]
is applied \(n\) steps late, and the first \(n-1\) steps of an episode make no update at all.
We will work through every section of the chapter including:
Four environments are used in this chapter:
All are finite MDPs, so we can always compute the exact answer with dynamic programming and grade the learner against it.

As we have done in prior chapters we will have one container hold everything that an algorithm might need.

NEG_INF = -1e30   # stand-in for -inf when masking illegal actions

@dataclass
class Env:
    name: str
    n_states: int
    n_actions: int
    P: np.ndarray              # (n_states, n_actions, n_states) transition probabilities
    reward_mean: np.ndarray    # (n_states, n_actions)
    reward_sd: np.ndarray      # (n_states, n_actions)
    terminal: np.ndarray       # (n_states,) bool
    start: np.ndarray          # (n_states,) start-state distribution
    legal_actions: np.ndarray  # (n_states, n_actions) 1.0 where the action is allowed
    reachable: np.ndarray      # (n_states,) reachable from a start state
    shape: tuple = ()          # grid shape, for printing


def make_env(name, n_states, n_actions, step_fn, terminals, starts, shape=(), legal_actions=None):
    """Build a tabular `Env` by asking a step function about every (s, a) pair.

    Terminal states absorb: every action leaves a terminal state where it is, with reward 0.
    The reachable states are found by a breadth-first search from the start states that
    follows only legal actions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Label for the environment. It also keys the DP oracle and names random generators.
    n_states, n_actions : int
        Number of states and of actions.
    step_fn : callable
        ``step_fn(s, a)`` returns ``(s_next, reward_mean, reward_sd)`` for one deterministic
        transition. It is never called on a terminal state.
    terminals : iterable of int
        The terminal states.
    starts : iterable of int
        The start states. Each episode starts in one of them, chosen uniformly.
    shape : tuple of int, default ()
        ``(n_rows, n_cols)`` of the grid. Used only for drawing.
    legal_actions : ndarray, shape (n_states, n_actions), optional
        1.0 where an action is allowed, 0.0 where it is not. By default every action is legal.

    Returns
    -------
    Env
        The model ``P`` (n_states, n_actions, n_states), the reward mean and standard
        deviation (n_states, n_actions), and the terminal, start, legal-action and
        reachable arrays.
    """
    P = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions, n_states))
    reward_mean = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    reward_sd = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    terminal = np.zeros(n_states, dtype=bool); terminal[list(terminals)] = True

    for s in range(n_states):
        for a in range(n_actions):
            if terminal[s]:
                P[s, a, s] = 1.0
                continue
            s_next, mean, sd = step_fn(s, a)
            P[s, a, s_next] = 1.0
            reward_mean[s, a] = mean
            reward_sd[s, a] = sd

    start = np.zeros(n_states)
    start[list(starts)] = 1.0 / len(list(starts))

    if legal_actions is None:
        legal_actions = np.ones((n_states, n_actions))

    reachable = start > 0 # Breadth-First-Search over the legal actions
    legal_P = P * (legal_actions > 0)[:, :, None] # illegal (s, a) rows zeroed out
    while True:
        frontier = legal_P[reachable & ~terminal] # transitions out of reachable, non-terminal states
        one_step_reachable = frontier.sum(axis=(0, 1)) > 0
        grown = reachable | one_step_reachable
        if grown.sum() == reachable.sum(): # No new states are reachable
            break
        reachable = grown

    return Env(name, n_states, n_actions, P, reward_mean, reward_sd, terminal, start,
               legal_actions, reachable, shape)


UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT = 0, 1, 2, 3
STEP = {UP: (0, 1), DOWN: (0, -1), LEFT: (-1, 0), RIGHT: (1, 0)}   # action -> (dx, dy) when drawn

def _move(row, col, action, n_rows, n_cols):
    """Move one cell on a grid. A move off the edge leaves the agent where it is.

    Parameters
    ----------
    row, col : int
        The current cell. Row 0 is the top row.
    action : {UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT}
        The direction to move.
    n_rows, n_cols : int
        Size of the grid.

    Returns
    -------
    row, col : int
        The cell after the move.
    """
    if action == UP: row = max(row - 1, 0)
    elif action == DOWN: row = min(row + 1, n_rows - 1)
    elif action == LEFT: col = max(col - 1, 0)
    elif action == RIGHT: col = min(col + 1, n_cols - 1)
    return row, col

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GridTheme:
    template: str    # plotly template
    background: str  # plot background, which shows in the gaps between cells
    floor: str       # fill of a non-terminal cell the agent can stand on
    wall: str        # fill of a cell the agent can never stand on

GRID_LIGHT = GridTheme(template="plotly_white", background="white", floor="#f2f2f2", wall="#9a9a9a")
GRID_DARK = GridTheme(template="plotly_dark", background="black", floor="#9e9d9d", wall="#4f4f4f")
GRID_TERMINAL = colors[4] # terminal cell fill, the same in both themes
GRID_INK, GRID_ARROW = "#4a4a4a", colors[2] # labels and policy arrows, drawn on the cells in both themes

def grid_xy(s, shape):
    """Convert a state id to (x, y) plot coordinates, with grid row 0 drawn at the top.

    Parameters
    ----------
    s : int
        The state, numbered ``row * n_cols + col``.
    shape : tuple of (int, int)
        The grid's (n_rows, n_cols).

    Returns
    -------
    x, y : int
        The column, and the row counted up from the bottom.
    """
    n_rows, n_cols = shape
    row, col = divmod(int(s), n_cols)
    return col, n_rows - 1 - row

def grid_panels(panel_titles, shape, title="", n_panel_cols=None, cell_px=100, theme=GRID_LIGHT):
    """Make an empty figure with one subplot per panel, each holding a grid of square cells.

    The figure is tall enough for every cell to be ``cell_px`` pixels high and takes the page
    width; the cells stay square. The panels are laid out left to right, then top to bottom.

    Parameters
    ----------
    panel_titles : list of str
        One title per panel.
    shape : tuple of (int, int)
        The (n_rows, n_cols) of the grid. Every panel shares it.
    title : str, default ""
        The figure title. Plotly HTML (<b>, <br>, <sup>) works.
    n_panel_cols : int, optional
        Panels per row of the figure. The default puts every panel in one row.
    cell_px : int, default 100
        Height of one grid cell, in pixels.
    theme : GridTheme, default GRID_LIGHT
        The plotly template and plot background. GRID_DARK for the book's dark theme.

    Returns
    -------
    plotly.graph_objects.Figure
        The figure, with the axes of every panel hidden and scaled so the cells are square.
    """
    n_rows, n_cols = shape
    n_panels = len(panel_titles)
    n_panel_cols = n_panel_cols or n_panels
    n_panel_rows = -(-n_panels // n_panel_cols) # ceiling division
    gap_x_px, gap_y_px = 20, 40 # between panels
    plot_width = n_panel_cols * n_cols * cell_px + (n_panel_cols - 1) * gap_x_px
    plot_height = n_panel_rows * n_rows * cell_px + (n_panel_rows - 1) * gap_y_px

    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=n_panel_rows,
        cols=n_panel_cols,
        subplot_titles=[f"<b>{t}</b>" for t in panel_titles],
        horizontal_spacing=gap_x_px / plot_width,
        vertical_spacing=gap_y_px / plot_height
    )

    for row in range(1, n_panel_rows + 1):
        for col in range(1, n_panel_cols + 1):
            x_axis = fig.get_subplot(row, col).xaxis.plotly_name.replace("axis", "")
            fig.update_xaxes(range=[-0.55, n_cols - 0.45], visible=False, constrain="domain",
                             row=row, col=col)
            fig.update_yaxes(range=[-0.55, n_rows - 0.45], visible=False, scaleanchor=x_axis,
                             constrain="domain", row=row, col=col)

    margin = dict(l=10, r=10, b=10, t=(80 if title else 0) + 30)
    fig.update_layout(
        title=title,
        height=plot_height + margin["t"] + margin["b"],
        margin=margin,
        template=theme.template,
        plot_bgcolor=theme.background,
        showlegend=False
    )
    return fig

def draw_cells(fig, env, fills, labels, row=1, col=1, pad=0.04):
    """Draw one filled square per state into a subplot, with an optional label on top.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fig : plotly.graph_objects.Figure
        A figure from `grid_panels`. It is changed in place.
    env : Env
        Supplies the grid shape.
    fills : list of str, length n_states
        The fill color of each state's cell.
    labels : dict of {int: str}
        Text drawn in the middle of a cell, by state, e.g. ``{start: "S"}``.
    row, col : int, default 1, 1
        The panel to draw into.
    pad : float, default 0.04
        Gap around each cell, in cell widths.
    """
    for s in range(env.n_states):
        x, y = grid_xy(s, env.shape)
        fig.add_shape(
            type="rect",
            x0=x - 0.5 + pad,
            x1=x + 0.5 - pad,
            y0=y - 0.5 + pad,
            y1=y + 0.5 - pad,
            fillcolor=fills[s],
            line_width=0,
            layer="below",
            row=row, col=col
        )
    for s, label in labels.items():
        x, y = grid_xy(s, env.shape)
        fig.add_annotation(x=x, y=y, text=f"<b>{label}</b>", showarrow=False,
                           font=dict(size=14, color=GRID_INK), row=row, col=col)

The four environments. All are undiscounted (\(\gamma = 1\)).

walk19: Nineteen states in a row, absorbing on both ends, \(-1\) for stepping off the left end and \(+1\) off the right, always starting in the center.
room: A \(6\times10\) open room, every reward \(0\) except \(+1\) for reaching the goal in the top-right corner.
windy: a \(7\times10\) grid with an upward wind of 0-2 cells depending on the column you leave from, \(-1\) per step.
cliff: a \(4\times12\) grid where stepping into the bottom-row cliff costs \(-100\) and teleports you back to the start.


def walk_env(n_walk=19, left_end_reward=-1.0, right_end_reward=1.0):
    """Build a random walk on ``n_walk`` states in a row, with absorbing ends.

    Stepping off the left end earns ``left_end_reward``, stepping off the right end
    ``right_end_reward``, and every other step 0. Every episode starts in the middle state.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_walk : int, default 19
        Number of non-terminal states. Use an odd number so there is a middle state.
    left_end_reward, right_end_reward : float, default -1.0, 1.0
        Rewards for stepping off the left end and off the right end.

    Returns
    -------
    Env
        The walk, with ``n_walk + 2`` states (the two ends included) and 2 actions: 0 steps
        left, 1 steps right.
    """
    n_states = n_walk + 2
    def step(s, a): # a = 0 left, a = 1 right
        """The step function for `make_env`: one step left or right.

        Parameters
        ----------
        s : int
            The current state, 1 to ``n_walk``.
        a : {0, 1}
            0 steps left, 1 steps right.

        Returns
        -------
        s_next : int
            The next state.
        reward_mean : float
            ``left_end_reward`` for the step into the left end, ``right_end_reward`` into the
            right end, 0.0 otherwise.
        reward_sd : float
            0.0: the reward has no noise.
        """
        s_next = s - 1 if a == 0 else s + 1
        return s_next, (left_end_reward if s_next == 0 else right_end_reward if s_next == n_states - 1 else 0.0), 0.0
    return make_env(f"walk{n_walk}", n_states, 2, step, [0, n_states - 1],
                    [(n_states - 1) // 2], shape=(1, n_states))

def room_env(n_rows=6, n_cols=10, goal_reward=1.0):
    """Build Figure 7.4's board: an open room with the goal in the top-right corner.

    Every reward is 0 except ``goal_reward`` for the step into the goal, so until an episode
    reaches G there is nothing at all to learn. Episodes start in the bottom-left corner. Moves
    are deterministic, and a move into the wall leaves the agent where it is.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_rows, n_cols : int, default 6, 10
        Size of the room.
    goal_reward : float, default 1.0
        Reward for the step into the goal.

    Returns
    -------
    Env
        The room, with 4 actions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT).
    """
    goal = n_cols - 1
    start = (n_rows - 1) * n_cols
    def step(s, a):
        """The step function for `make_env`: one deterministic move.

        Parameters
        ----------
        s : int
            The current state, numbered ``row * n_cols + col``.
        a : {UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT}
            The action.

        Returns
        -------
        s_next : int
            The next state.
        reward_mean : float
            ``goal_reward`` for the step into the goal, 0.0 otherwise.
        reward_sd : float
            0.0: the reward has no noise.
        """
        row, col = _move(*divmod(s, n_cols), a, n_rows, n_cols)
        s_next = row * n_cols + col
        return s_next, (goal_reward if s_next == goal else 0.0), 0.0
    return make_env("room", n_rows * n_cols, 4, step, [goal], [start], shape=(n_rows, n_cols))


WIND = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 0])

def windy_env(n_rows=7, n_cols=10, step_reward=-1.0):
    """Build the windy gridworld.

    After each move, the wind of the column the agent leaves, ``WIND[col]``, pushes it that many
    rows up, stopping at the top edge. Episodes start at row 3, column 0, and the goal is row 3,
    column 7. Every step earns ``step_reward``, without noise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_rows, n_cols : int, default 7, 10
        Size of the grid.
    step_reward : float, default -1.0
        Reward on every step.

    Returns
    -------
    Env
        The gridworld, with 4 actions.
    """
    def step(s, a):
        """The step function for `make_env`: one move, then the wind.

        Parameters
        ----------
        s : int
            The current state, numbered ``row * n_cols + col``.
        a : {UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT}
            The action.

        Returns
        -------
        s_next : int
            The next state.
        reward_mean : float
            ``step_reward`` on every step.
        reward_sd : float
            0.0: the reward has no noise.
        """
        row, col = divmod(s, n_cols)
        row_next, col_next = _move(row, col, a, n_rows, n_cols)
        row_next = max(row_next - WIND[col], 0)   # wind of the column you leave, blowing up
        return row_next * n_cols + col_next, step_reward, 0.0
    return make_env("windy", n_rows * n_cols, 4, step, [3 * n_cols + 7], [3 * n_cols],
                    shape=(n_rows, n_cols))

def cliff_env(n_rows=4, n_cols=12, step_reward=-1.0, cliff_reward=-100.0):
    """Build the cliff-walking gridworld.

    The start and the goal are the two bottom corners, and the cells between them are the cliff.
    Stepping into the cliff earns ``cliff_reward`` and sends the agent back to the start, without
    ending the episode, so the cliff cells themselves are never occupied. Every other step earns
    ``step_reward``. Rewards have no noise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_rows, n_cols : int, default 4, 12
        Size of the grid.
    step_reward : float, default -1.0
        Reward for a step that does not enter the cliff.
    cliff_reward : float, default -100.0
        Reward for stepping into the cliff.

    Returns
    -------
    Env
        The gridworld, with 4 actions.
    """
    start_state = (n_rows - 1) * n_cols
    goal = (n_rows - 1) * n_cols + n_cols - 1
    cliff_cells = {(n_rows - 1) * n_cols + col for col in range(1, n_cols - 1)}
    def step(s, a):
        """The step function for `make_env`: one move, or a fall into the cliff.

        Parameters
        ----------
        s : int
            The current state, numbered ``row * n_cols + col``.
        a : {UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT}
            The action.

        Returns
        -------
        s_next : int
            The next state: the start state after a fall.
        reward_mean : float
            ``cliff_reward`` for a fall into the cliff, ``step_reward`` otherwise.
        reward_sd : float
            0.0: the reward has no noise.
        """
        row, col = _move(*divmod(s, n_cols), a, n_rows, n_cols)
        s_next = row * n_cols + col
        return (start_state, cliff_reward, 0.0) if s_next in cliff_cells else (s_next, step_reward, 0.0)
    return make_env("cliff", n_rows * n_cols, 4, step, [goal], [start_state],
                    shape=(n_rows, n_cols))

walk19, room, windy, cliff = walk_env(19), room_env(), windy_env(), cliff_env()

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
The DP oracle
The same DP Oracle deal we have been implementing across the last few chapters.

def make_dp(env, n_iters=2000):
    """Compile exact dynamic programming for one environment: the "DP oracle".

    Both solvers start from v = 0 and apply ``n_iters`` synchronous sweeps, with terminal
    states held at 0. Policy evaluation applies the Bellman expectation backup,

        v(s) <- sum_a pi(a|s) [ r(s, a) + gamma * sum_s' p(s'|s, a) v(s') ],

    and value iteration applies the Bellman optimality backup, a max over the legal actions
    in place of the sum over pi.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env : Env
        Supplies the model: ``P``, ``reward_mean``, ``terminal`` and ``legal_actions``.
    n_iters : int, default 2000
        Number of sweeps for each solver.

    Returns
    -------
    evaluate_policy : callable
        ``evaluate_policy(pi, gamma) -> v_pi``, with ``pi`` of shape (n_states, n_actions)
        and ``v_pi`` of shape (n_states,).
    optimal_values : callable
        ``optimal_values(gamma) -> v_*``, shape (n_states,).
    action_values_of : callable
        ``action_values_of(v, gamma) -> q``, the one-step lookahead
        ``q(s, a) = r(s, a) + gamma * sum_s' p(s'|s, a) v(s')``, shape (n_states, n_actions).
    """
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    legal_actions = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.legal_actions)
    gamma = pt.scalar("gamma")
    pi = pt.matrix("pi")
    v_in = pt.vector("v")

    def q_from(v, gamma):
        """One-step lookahead: turn state values into action values.

            q(s, a) = r(s, a) + gamma * sum_s' p(s'|s, a) v(s')

        Parameters
        ----------
        v : TensorVariable, shape (n_states,)
            State values.
        gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
            Discount factor.

        Returns
        -------
        TensorVariable, shape (n_states, n_actions)
            The action values q(s, a).
        """
        return reward + gamma * (P * v[None, None, :]).sum(axis=2)

    def expectation_step(v, pi, gamma):
        """One sweep of policy evaluation: v_{k+1}(s) = sum_a pi(a|s) q_k(s, a), terminals held at 0.

        Parameters
        ----------
        v : TensorVariable, shape (n_states,)
            The values v_k from the previous sweep.
        pi : TensorVariable, shape (n_states, n_actions)
            The policy pi(a|s).
        gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
            Discount factor.

        Returns
        -------
        TensorVariable, shape (n_states,)
            The values v_{k+1}.
        """
        return not_terminal * (pi * q_from(v, gamma)).sum(axis=1)

    def optimality_step(v, gamma):
        """One sweep of value iteration: v_{k+1}(s) = max over the legal a of q_k(s, a), terminals held at 0.

        Parameters
        ----------
        v : TensorVariable, shape (n_states,)
            The values v_k from the previous sweep.
        gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
            Discount factor.

        Returns
        -------
        TensorVariable, shape (n_states,)
            The values v_{k+1}.
        """
        q = pt.where(legal_actions > 0, q_from(v, gamma), NEG_INF)
        return not_terminal * q.max(axis=1)

    v_eval = pytensor.scan(
        fn=expectation_step,
        outputs_info=pt.zeros((env.n_states,)),
        non_sequences=[pi, gamma],
        n_steps=n_iters,
        return_updates=False
    )

    v_star = pytensor.scan(
        fn=optimality_step,
        outputs_info=pt.zeros((env.n_states,)),
        non_sequences=[gamma],
        n_steps=n_iters,
        return_updates=False
    )
    return (pytensor.function([pi, gamma], v_eval[-1]), # evaluate_policy
            pytensor.function([gamma], v_star[-1]), # optimal_values
            pytensor.function([v_in, gamma], q_from(v_in, gamma))) # action_values_of


GAMMA_WALK = 1.0 # every environment in this chapter is undiscounted
GAMMA_ROOM = 1.0
GAMMA_WINDY = 1.0
GAMMA_CLIFF = 1.0

ORACLE = {e.name: make_dp(e) for e in (walk19, room, windy, cliff)}

def exact(env, gamma, pi=None):
    """Return the exact state and action values from the DP oracle in ``ORACLE[env.name]``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env : Env
        The environment. Its oracle must already be in ``ORACLE``.
    gamma : float
        Discount factor.
    pi : ndarray, shape (n_states, n_actions), optional
        A policy, as pi(a|s). If given, return v_pi and q_pi; otherwise v_* and q_*.

    Returns
    -------
    v : ndarray, shape (n_states,)
        v_pi or v_*.
    q : ndarray, shape (n_states, n_actions)
        The matching action values, ``r(s, a) + gamma * sum_s' p(s'|s, a) v(s')``, set to 0
        in terminal states.
    """
    evaluate_policy, optimal_values, action_values_of = ORACLE[env.name]
    v = evaluate_policy(pi, gamma) if pi is not None else optimal_values(gamma)
    q = action_values_of(v, gamma)
    q[env.terminal] = 0.0
    return v, q

def greedy_pi(Q, env):
    """Return the deterministic greedy policy of a Q table, as a pi(a|s) matrix.

    Ties go to the lowest-numbered legal action.

    Parameters
    ----------
    Q : ndarray, shape (n_states, n_actions)
        Action values.
    env : Env
        Supplies the legal actions.

    Returns
    -------
    ndarray, shape (n_states, n_actions)
        1.0 on the greedy legal action of each state, 0.0 elsewhere.
    """
    pi = np.zeros((env.n_states, env.n_actions))
    pi[np.arange(env.n_states),
       np.where(env.legal_actions > 0, Q, NEG_INF).argmax(axis=1)] = 1.0
    return pi

inner_states = np.arange(1, 20)                       # the 19 non-terminal walk states
pi_walk = np.ones((walk19.n_states, 2)) / 2           # the equiprobable random policy
v_walk, _ = exact(walk19, GAMMA_WALK, pi_walk)

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
Simulator
Again same deal as before but now we need to pay a little more attention to the padding.
That padding does more work in this chapter than it did in the last one. An \(n\)-step window that starts before the episode ends will often extend past it, and the book handles this by truncating the return at \(T\). We get the same thing for free: past \(T\) the rewards are 0 and the bootstrap term is multiplied by \(\mathrm{not\_terminal}\), so \(G_{t:t+n}\) silently collapses to the full return \(G_t\) - with no special case in the code. The one thing we owe it is enough room: episodes must finish at least \(n\) steps before max_steps, and every experiment below reports what fraction actually did.

def make_rollout(env, seed):
    """Compile a batched episode simulator for one environment.

    Rolls out many episodes in parallel for ``max_steps`` steps each, under a behavior policy b.
    At every step,

        A_t ~ b(. | S_t),    S_{t+1} ~ p(. | S_t, A_t),    R_{t+1} ~ N(r_mu(S_t, A_t), r_sigma(S_t, A_t)).

    Terminal states absorb with reward 0, so the steps after an episode ends are padding. The
    random generator state carries over between calls.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env : Env
        Supplies the model: ``P``, ``reward_mean`` and ``reward_sd``.
    seed : int
        Seed for the simulator's random generator.

    Returns
    -------
    callable
        Compiled PyTensor function ``(b, s_start, max_steps) -> (S, A, R, S_next)``. ``b`` has
        shape (n_states, n_actions) and ``s_start`` is int64 of shape (n_episodes,). Each output
        has shape (max_steps, n_episodes), and row t holds S_t, A_t, R_{t+1} and S_{t+1}.
    """
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward_mean = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    reward_sd = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_sd)
    rng_shared = pt.random.shared_rng(seed=seed, name=f"rng_roll_{env.name}")
    pi = pt.matrix("pi")
    s_start = pt.lvector("s0")
    max_steps = pt.iscalar("T")

    def step(s, rng, pi):
        """Advance every episode by one time step: draw A_t, then S_{t+1} and R_{t+1}.

        Parameters
        ----------
        s : TensorVariable of int, shape (n_episodes,)
            The current states S_t.
        rng : RandomGeneratorSharedVariable
            The random generator state, threaded through the scan.
        pi : TensorVariable, shape (n_states, n_actions)
            The policy being rolled out (the behavior policy b).

        Returns
        -------
        s_next : TensorVariable of int, shape (n_episodes,)
            The next states S_{t+1}.
        rng : RandomGeneratorSharedVariable
            The advanced generator.
        a : TensorVariable of int, shape (n_episodes,)
            The actions A_t.
        r : TensorVariable, shape (n_episodes,)
            The rewards R_{t+1}.
        """
        rng, a = rng.categorical(p=pi[s]) # A_t ~ b(.|S_t)
        rng, s_next = rng.categorical(p=P[s, a]) # S_{t+1} ~ p(.|S_t,A_t)
        rng, r = rng.normal(loc=reward_mean[s, a], scale=reward_sd[s, a]) # R_{t+1}
        return s_next, rng, a, r

    S_next, rng_final, A, R = pytensor.scan(
        fn=step,
        outputs_info=[s_start, rng_shared, None, None],
        non_sequences=[pi],
        n_steps=max_steps,
        return_updates=False
    )
    S = pt.concatenate([s_start[None, :], S_next[:-1]], axis=0) # row t = S_t
    return pytensor.function([pi, s_start, max_steps], [S, A, R, S_next],
                             updates={rng_shared: rng_final})

def episodes_for(rollout, env, b, n_episodes, n_learners, max_steps, pi=None):
    """Simulate a stream of episodes for every learner under the behavior policy b, in one rollout call.

    Start states are drawn from ``env.start``. The (max_steps, n_episodes * n_learners) rollout is
    reshaped to (n_episodes, max_steps, n_learners), so that learner r sees its own stream of
    ``n_episodes`` episodes in order. The importance ratio at each step is

        rho_t = pi(A_t | S_t) / b(A_t | S_t),

    set to 1 on the padded steps past termination, and everywhere when no target policy is given.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rollout : callable
        A simulator from `make_rollout` for ``env``.
    env : Env
        Supplies the start-state distribution and the terminal states.
    b : ndarray, shape (n_states, n_actions)
        The behavior policy that generates the episodes.
    n_episodes : int
        Episodes per learner.
    n_learners : int
        Number of independent learners.
    max_steps : int
        Steps per episode. An episode that has not terminated by then is cut off.
    pi : ndarray, shape (n_states, n_actions), optional
        The target policy. If omitted, every ratio is 1 (on-policy).

    Returns
    -------
    S, A, R, rho : ndarray, shape (n_episodes, max_steps, n_learners)
        The states, actions, rewards R_{t+1} and importance ratios at every step.
    frac_finished : float
        The fraction of episodes that reached a terminal state within ``max_steps``.
    """
    n_chains = n_episodes * n_learners
    s_start = np_rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(env.start > 0), size=n_chains,
                            p=env.start[env.start > 0]).astype("int64")
    S, A, R, S_next = rollout(b, s_start, max_steps)
    by_episode = lambda X: X.reshape(max_steps, n_episodes, n_learners).transpose(1, 0, 2)
    S, A, R = by_episode(S), by_episode(A), by_episode(R)
    rho = np.ones_like(R) if pi is None else pi[S, A] / b[S, A]
    rho[env.terminal[S]] = 1.0
    return S, A, R, rho, env.terminal[S_next[-1]].mean()

np_rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
rollout_walk = make_rollout(walk19, 2026)

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
The update as a scan
The book’s pseudocode keeps a rolling buffer of the last \(n\) states and rewards and, at each step \(t\), updates the state \(\tau = t - n + 1\). When the transitions are already recorded there is no buffer to manage: pytensor.scan walks \(\tau\) itself and slices the window \(S_\tau\ldots S_{\tau+n}\), \(R_{\tau+1}\ldots R_{\tau+n}\) straight out of the episode, stopping at \(\tau = T - n\) rather than running off the end of the array.
The V carried through the scan at iteration \(\tau\) is the one produced by all the updates for \(\tau' < \tau\), which are the updates made at times up to \(\tau + n - 1\). That is exactly the book’s \(V_{t+n-1}\), so the online character of the algorithm is preserved rather than approximated.

def make_n_step_predict(env, n, kind="on_policy"):
    """Compile n-step TD prediction for many learners at once: on-policy, or off-policy two ways.

    Each learner walks its own episodes in order. At each time tau it updates the state S_tau
    from the window S_tau .. S_{tau+n}, R_{tau+1} .. R_{tau+n},

        V(S_tau) <- V(S_tau) + alpha * weight * [ G - V(S_tau) ],

    where, with V of a terminal state counted as 0,

    - 'on_policy': ``G = G_{tau:tau+n} = sum_{k<n} gamma^k R_{tau+k+1} + gamma^n V(S_{tau+n})``,
      weight 1;
    - 'importance_sampling': the same G, ``weight = rho_{tau:tau+n-1}``, the product of the
      window's ratios;
    - 'control_variates': weight 1, and the per-decision return built backward from
      ``G_{h:h} = V(S_h)`` with ``G_{j:h} = rho_j (R_{j+1} + gamma G_{j+1:h}) + (1 - rho_j) V(S_j)``.

    Past the end of an episode the rewards are 0 and V of the terminal state is 0, so the
    n-step return collapses to the full return, and states after termination are not updated.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env : Env
        Supplies the terminal states.
    n : int
        Number of steps in the return.
    kind : {'on_policy', 'importance_sampling', 'control_variates'}, default 'on_policy'
        Which return and weight to use.

    Returns
    -------
    callable
        Compiled PyTensor function ``(S, R, rho, V_init, alpha, gamma) -> V``:

        - ``S``: int64, shape (n_episodes, max_steps, n_learners).
        - ``R``, ``rho``: shape (n_episodes, max_steps, n_learners), the rewards R_{t+1} and the
          importance ratios (all 1 on-policy).
        - ``V_init``: shape (n_learners, n_states).
        - ``alpha``: shape (n_learners,), each learner's step size, which is how the step-size
          sweeps run as one call.
        - ``gamma``: float, the discount factor.
        - ``V``: shape (n_episodes, n_learners, n_states), the values after each episode.
    """
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    S_all = pt.ltensor3("S")
    R_all = pt.dtensor3("R")
    rho_all = pt.dtensor3("rho")
    V_init = pt.dmatrix("V0")
    alpha = pt.dvector("alpha")
    gamma = pt.scalar("g")
    gamma_powers = (gamma ** pt.arange(n + 1))[:, None] # gamma^0 .. gamma^n

    def transition(tau, V, S_ep, R_ep, rho_ep, alpha, gamma, gamma_powers):
        """Apply the update at time tau, for every learner.

        The window is sliced out of the episode. For control variates the return over it is
        scanned rather than unrolled, so the graph is the same size whatever n is.

        Parameters
        ----------
        tau : TensorVariable of int, scalar
            The time whose state is updated, supplied by the scan sequence.
        V : TensorVariable, shape (n_learners, n_states)
            The values before the update: the book's V_{tau+n-1}.
        S_ep : TensorVariable of int, shape (max_steps, n_learners)
            One episode's states.
        R_ep, rho_ep : TensorVariable, shape (max_steps, n_learners)
            Its rewards R_{t+1} and importance ratios.
        alpha : TensorVariable, shape (n_learners,)
            Each learner's step size.
        gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
            Discount factor.
        gamma_powers : TensorVariable, shape (n + 1, 1)
            gamma^0 .. gamma^n.

        Returns
        -------
        TensorVariable, shape (n_learners, n_states)
            The values after the update. Only V(S_tau) changes, and not at all once the episode
            has ended.
        """
        S_win = S_ep[tau:tau + n + 1] # S_tau .. S_{tau+n}, (n+1, n_learners)
        R_win = R_ep[tau:tau + n] # R_{tau+1} .. R_{tau+n}, (n, n_learners)
        rho_win = rho_ep[tau:tau + n] # rho_tau .. rho_{tau+n-1}, (n, n_learners)

        learners = pt.arange(V.shape[0])
        V_win = not_terminal[S_win] * V[learners, S_win]  # V(S_tau..S_{tau+n}), 0 at terminals
        s_tau = S_win[0]
        still_running = not_terminal[s_tau] # no update once the episode has ended

        if kind == "control_variates":

            def down_one_level(rho_j, R_j, V_j, G, gamma):
                """One level of the per-decision return with control variates, walking backward.

                    G_{j:h} = rho_j (R_{j+1} + gamma G_{j+1:h}) + (1 - rho_j) V(S_j)

                Parameters
                ----------
                rho_j : TensorVariable, shape (n_learners,)
                    The importance ratio at time j, supplied by the scan sequence.
                R_j : TensorVariable, shape (n_learners,)
                    The reward R_{j+1}, supplied by the scan sequence.
                V_j : TensorVariable, shape (n_learners,)
                    V(S_j), 0 at a terminal state, supplied by the scan sequence.
                G : TensorVariable, shape (n_learners,)
                    The return one level down, G_{j+1:h}.
                gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
                    Discount factor.

                Returns
                -------
                TensorVariable, shape (n_learners,)
                    The return G_{j:h}.
                """
                return rho_j * (R_j + gamma * G) + (1 - rho_j) * V_j

            G_levels = pytensor.scan( # from the base case back up to tau
                fn=down_one_level,
                sequences=[rho_win[::-1], R_win[::-1], V_win[:n][::-1]],
                outputs_info=V_win[n], # G_{h:h} = V(S_h)
                non_sequences=[gamma],
                return_updates=False)
            G, weight = G_levels[-1], 1.0
        else:
            G = (gamma_powers[:n] * R_win).sum(axis=0) + gamma_powers[n] * V_win[n]
            weight = rho_win.prod(axis=0) if kind == "importance_sampling" else 1.0

        return pt.inc_subtensor(V[learners, s_tau],
                                alpha * still_running * weight * (G - V[learners, s_tau]))

    def episode(S_ep, R_ep, rho_ep, V, alpha, gamma, gamma_powers):
        """Run `transition` for tau = 0 .. max_steps - n - 1 over one episode, in order.

        Parameters
        ----------
        S_ep : TensorVariable of int, shape (max_steps, n_learners)
            One episode's states, supplied by the outer scan sequence.
        R_ep, rho_ep : TensorVariable, shape (max_steps, n_learners)
            Its rewards R_{t+1} and importance ratios.
        V : TensorVariable, shape (n_learners, n_states)
            The values before this episode.
        alpha : TensorVariable, shape (n_learners,)
            Each learner's step size.
        gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
            Discount factor.
        gamma_powers : TensorVariable, shape (n + 1, 1)
            gamma^0 .. gamma^n.

        Returns
        -------
        TensorVariable, shape (n_learners, n_states)
            The values after this episode.
        """
        V_steps = pytensor.scan(
            fn=transition,
            sequences=pt.arange(S_ep.shape[0] - n), # tau = 0 .. max_steps-n-1
            outputs_info=V,
            non_sequences=[S_ep, R_ep, rho_ep, alpha, gamma, gamma_powers],
            return_updates=False
        )
        return V_steps[-1]

    V_per_episode = pytensor.scan(
        fn=episode,
        sequences=[S_all, R_all, rho_all],
        outputs_info=V_init,
        non_sequences=[alpha, gamma, gamma_powers],
        return_updates=False
    )
    return pytensor.function([S_all, R_all, rho_all, V_init, alpha, gamma], V_per_episode)

The panel on the left shows the mechanism and the one on the right shows the trade-off. Notice the following:

One-step TD moves exactly one state per episode. The reward is non-zero only at the two ends, so \(n=1\) leaves 18 of the 19 states at zero after the first episode. \(n=16\) moves seven states, and moves them toward the oracle value. This is why \(n\)-step methods learn faster early.
Every curve is a U in \(\alpha\), and the best \(\alpha\) falls as \(n\) grows. A larger \(n\) means the target sums more sampled rewards, so it carries more variance, so it can tolerate a smaller step.
The best \(n\) is in the middle.

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
The scan update for control
Now that the behavior policy depends on \(Q\), we can no longer pre-generate the whole episode and just slice through it. Instead, we keep a rolling buffer of three arrays \((S, A, R)\) of shape (n_runs, n) that slide one column per step, ensuring that after the step at time \(t\) they hold \(S_\tau\ldots S_{t}\), \(A_\tau\ldots A_t\) and \(R_{\tau+1}\ldots R_{t+1}\) for \(\tau = t-n+1\). That is one column short of the window: the live pair \((S_{t+1}, A_{t+1})\) supplies \(S_{\tau+n}\) and \(A_{\tau+n}\), which is why \(A_{t+1}\) is drawn before the update fires.
The buffers are initialized to a terminal state, so the mask that suppresses updates past the end of an episode also suppresses the first \(n-1\) steps, when the window has not yet filled. Every \(Q\) term in each return is read off the current \(Q\), which corresponds to the book’s \(Q_{\tau+n-1}\).
The following sections differ only in the return, so we write the returns once, as a single function, and let the control loop stay fixed. Only the first two branches are used in this section.

def eps_greedy_probs(legal, q, eps):
    """Return the ε-greedy distribution over the legal actions of s, for every run.

        pi(a|s) = 1 - eps + eps / n_legal   for the greedy legal action,
                  eps / n_legal             for every other legal action,
                  0                         for an illegal action.

    Ties for the greedy action go to the lowest-numbered action.

    Parameters
    ----------
    legal : TensorVariable, shape (..., n_runs, n_actions)
        1.0 where an action is legal in each run's state, optionally with leading axes (e.g. the
        levels of a window).
    q : TensorVariable, shape (..., n_runs, n_actions)
        The action values in those states.
    eps : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
        Each run's ε.

    Returns
    -------
    TensorVariable, shape (..., n_runs, n_actions)
        The action probabilities in each state.
    """
    greedy = pt.argmax(pt.where(legal > 0, q, NEG_INF), axis=-1)
    probs = legal * (eps / legal.sum(axis=-1))[..., None]
    one_hot = pt.eq(pt.arange(legal.shape[-1]), greedy[..., None])
    return probs + one_hot * (1.0 - eps)[:, None]


def n_step_return(env, kind, n, Q, S_win, A_win, R_win, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma):
    """Return the n-step action-value return over one window, and the weight on its update.

    Every Q term is read off the current Q, which is the book's Q_{h-1}, and a terminal state
    contributes 0. With ``h = tau + n``:

    - 'sarsa': ``G = sum_{k<n} gamma^k R_{tau+k+1} + gamma^n Q(S_h, A_h)``, weight 1.
    - 'expected_sarsa': the same rewards ``+ gamma^n V-bar(S_h)``, where
      ``V-bar(s) = sum_a pi(a|s) Q(s, a)`` under the target policy, weight 1.
    - 'off_policy_sarsa': the Sarsa G, weighted by ``rho_{tau+1:tau+n}``, the product of
      pi(A|S) / b(A|S) over the window after A_tau.
    - 'q_sigma': weight 1, and G built backward from ``G_{h:h} = Q(S_h, A_h)`` with

          G_{j-1} = R_j + gamma c_j (G_j - Q(S_j, A_j)) + gamma V-bar(S_j),
          c_j = sigma rho_j + (1 - sigma) pi(A_j | S_j).

      sigma = 0 gives tree backup, sigma = 1 per-decision importance sampling with control
      variates.

    The target policy is ``eps_target``-greedy in Q and the behavior policy ``eps_behavior``-greedy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env : Env
        Supplies the terminal states and the legal actions.
    kind : {'sarsa', 'expected_sarsa', 'off_policy_sarsa', 'q_sigma'}
        Which return to form.
    n : int
        Number of steps in the return.
    Q : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs, n_states, n_actions)
        The current action values.
    S_win, A_win : TensorVariable of int, shape (n + 1, n_runs)
        The windows S_tau .. S_{tau+n} and A_tau .. A_{tau+n}.
    R_win : TensorVariable, shape (n, n_runs)
        The rewards R_{tau+1} .. R_{tau+n}.
    eps_behavior, eps_target : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
        Each run's behavior and target ε.
    sigma : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
        Each run's degree of sampling, used only by 'q_sigma'.
    gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
        Discount factor.

    Returns
    -------
    G : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
        The return.
    weight : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,), or float
        The importance weight on the update: ``rho_{tau+1:tau+n}`` for 'off_policy_sarsa',
        1.0 otherwise.
    """
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    legal_actions = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.legal_actions)
    runs = pt.arange(Q.shape[0])
    gamma_powers = (gamma ** pt.arange(n + 1))[:, None]

    def at(s, a):
        """Look up every per-level quantity the returns need, for (state, action) pairs.

        Parameters
        ----------
        s, a : TensorVariable of int, shape (..., n_runs)
            States and actions, e.g. one level of the window or several stacked.

        Returns
        -------
        dict of {str: TensorVariable of shape (..., n_runs)}
            - ``'q'``: Q(s, a), 0 at a terminal state.
            - ``'q_bar'``: V-bar(s) = sum_a' pi(a'|s) Q(s, a') under the target policy, 0 at a
              terminal state.
            - ``'pi_a'``: pi(a|s), the target policy's probability of a.
            - ``'rho'``: pi(a|s) / b(a|s), set to 1 at a terminal state.
        """
        live = not_terminal[s]
        pi_probs = eps_greedy_probs(legal_actions[s], Q[runs, s], eps_target)
        b_probs = eps_greedy_probs(legal_actions[s], Q[runs, s], eps_behavior)
        take = lambda probs: pt.take_along_axis(probs, a[..., None], axis=-1)[..., 0]
        pi_a = take(pi_probs)
        b_a = take(b_probs)
        return dict(
            q=live * Q[runs, s, a], # Q(S, A)
            q_bar=live * (pi_probs * Q[runs, s]).sum(axis=-1), # V-bar(S)
            pi_a=pi_a, # pi(A | S)
            rho=1.0 + live * (pi_a / b_a - 1.0)) # 1 when not live and minus 1 to counter the added 1

    if kind == "q_sigma":
        step = at(S_win[1:], A_win[1:]) # levels tau+1 .. tau+n, valued in one go
        c = sigma * step["rho"] + (1 - sigma) * step["pi_a"]  # control variate

        def down_one_level(R_j, c_j, q_j, q_bar_j, G, gamma):
            """One level of the Q(sigma) return, walking backward.

                G_{j-1} = R_j + gamma c_j (G_j - Q(S_j, A_j)) + gamma V-bar(S_j)

            Parameters
            ----------
            R_j : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
                The reward R_j, supplied by the scan sequence.
            c_j : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
                ``sigma rho_j + (1 - sigma) pi(A_j | S_j)``, supplied by the scan sequence.
            q_j : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
                Q(S_j, A_j), supplied by the scan sequence.
            q_bar_j : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
                V-bar(S_j), supplied by the scan sequence.
            G : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
                The return one level down, G_j.
            gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
                Discount factor.

            Returns
            -------
            TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
                The return G_{j-1}.
            """
            return R_j + gamma * c_j * (G - q_j) + gamma * q_bar_j

        G_levels = pytensor.scan(
            fn=down_one_level,
            sequences=[R_win[::-1], c[::-1], step["q"][::-1], step["q_bar"][::-1]],
            outputs_info=step["q"][n - 1],  # G_{h:h} = Q(S_h, A_h)
            non_sequences=[gamma],
            return_updates=False)
        return G_levels[-1], 1.0

    if kind == "off_policy_sarsa":
        step = at(S_win[1:], A_win[1:])
        bootstrap, weight = step["q"][n - 1], step["rho"].prod(axis=0) # rho_{tau+1:tau+n}
    else:
        step = at(S_win[n], A_win[n])
        bootstrap = step["q_bar"] if kind == "expected_sarsa" else step["q"]
        weight = 1.0

    return (gamma_powers[:n] * R_win).sum(axis=0) + gamma_powers[n] * bootstrap, weight


def make_n_step_control(env, kind, n, seed):
    """Compile n-step tabular TD control for many runs at once, with the return chosen by ``kind``.

    The behavior policy is ``eps_behavior``-greedy in Q and the target policy ``eps_target``-greedy
    in Q, so equal ε make every method on-policy. Rolling buffers of the last n states, actions
    and rewards slide one column per step; with the live pair (S_{t+1}, A_{t+1}) they make up the
    window for tau = t - n + 1, and after every step

        Q(S_tau, A_tau) <- Q(S_tau, A_tau) + alpha * weight * [ G - Q(S_tau, A_tau) ],

    with G and weight from `n_step_return`. The buffers start out holding a terminal state, so the
    first n - 1 steps, before the window fills, and the steps after termination update nothing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env : Env
        Supplies the model the agent acts in, the legal actions and the start distribution.
    kind : {'sarsa', 'expected_sarsa', 'off_policy_sarsa', 'q_sigma'}
        Which return to use; see `n_step_return`.
    n : int
        Number of steps in the return.
    seed : int
        Seed for the random generator.

    Returns
    -------
    callable
        Compiled PyTensor function
        ``(Q_init, alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma, n_episodes, max_steps) -> (Q, reward_sum, step_count, done)``:

        - ``Q_init``: shape (n_runs, n_states, n_actions).
        - ``alpha``, ``eps_behavior``, ``eps_target``, ``sigma``: shape (n_runs,), which is how
          the sweeps run many settings as one batched call.
        - ``gamma``: float, the discount factor.
        - ``Q``: shape (n_runs, n_states, n_actions), the action values after the last episode.
        - ``reward_sum``, ``step_count``: shape (n_episodes, n_runs), each episode's sum of
          rewards and number of steps.
        - ``done``: shape (n_episodes, n_runs), 1.0 where the episode terminated within
          ``max_steps``.

        The random generator state carries over between calls.
    """
    P = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.P)
    reward_mean = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_mean)
    reward_sd = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.reward_sd)
    not_terminal = pt.as_tensor_variable((~env.terminal).astype("float64"))
    legal_actions = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.legal_actions)
    start_dist = pt.as_tensor_variable(env.start)
    pad_state = int(np.argmax(env.terminal))   # buffer filler: masks the first n-1 updates
    rng_shared = pt.random.shared_rng(seed=seed, name=f"rng_{kind}{n}_{env.name}")

    Q_init = pt.dtensor3("Q0")
    alpha = pt.dvector("alpha")
    eps_behavior = pt.dvector("eps_b")
    eps_target = pt.dvector("eps_pi")
    sigma = pt.dvector("sigma")
    gamma = pt.scalar("gamma")
    n_episodes = pt.iscalar("n_ep")
    max_steps = pt.iscalar("T")

    def pick(rng, Q, s, eps):
        """Draw one action per run from the ε-greedy policy of Q.

        Parameters
        ----------
        rng : RandomGeneratorSharedVariable
            The random generator state.
        Q : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs, n_states, n_actions)
            Action values.
        s : TensorVariable of int, shape (n_runs,)
            Each run's state.
        eps : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
            Each run's ε.

        Returns
        -------
        rng : RandomGeneratorSharedVariable
            The advanced generator.
        a : TensorVariable of int, shape (n_runs,)
            The actions.
        """
        runs = pt.arange(Q.shape[0])
        return rng.categorical(p=eps_greedy_probs(legal_actions[s], Q[runs, s], eps))

    def shift_in(buffer, x):
        """Slide a buffer one step: drop its oldest column and append x.

        Parameters
        ----------
        buffer : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs, n)
            The last n values, oldest first.
        x : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
            The newest value.

        Returns
        -------
        TensorVariable, shape (n_runs, n)
            The buffer after the slide.
        """
        return pt.concatenate([buffer[:, 1:], x[:, None]], axis=1)

    def inner(rng, s, a, live, S_buf, A_buf, R_buf, Q, reward_sum, step_count,
              alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma):
        """Take one step in every run, slide the buffers, and update Q(S_tau, A_tau).

        A_{t+1} is drawn before the update, because the window's last pair is (S_{t+1}, A_{t+1}).

        Parameters
        ----------
        rng : RandomGeneratorSharedVariable
            The random generator state.
        s, a : TensorVariable of int, shape (n_runs,)
            Each run's state S_t and action A_t.
        live : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
            1.0 while the run's episode has not terminated, 0.0 after.
        S_buf, A_buf : TensorVariable of int, shape (n_runs, n)
            The last n states and actions, oldest first.
        R_buf : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs, n)
            The last n rewards, oldest first.
        Q : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs, n_states, n_actions)
            Action values before the update.
        reward_sum, step_count : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
            The episode's sum of rewards and number of steps so far.
        alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
            Each run's settings.
        gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
            Discount factor.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple
            ``(rng, s_next, a_next, live, S_buf, A_buf, R_buf, Q, reward_sum, step_count)`` for the
            next step.
        """
        runs = pt.arange(Q.shape[0])
        rng, s_next = rng.categorical(p=P[s, a])
        rng, r = rng.normal(loc=reward_mean[s, a], scale=reward_sd[s, a])
        rng, a_next = pick(rng, Q, s_next, eps_behavior)   # A_{t+1}, drawn before the update

        S_buf, A_buf, R_buf = shift_in(S_buf, s), shift_in(A_buf, a), shift_in(R_buf, r)
        S_win = pt.concatenate([S_buf.T, s_next[None]])     # S_tau .. S_{tau+n}, (n+1, n_runs)
        A_win = pt.concatenate([A_buf.T, a_next[None]])     # A_tau .. A_{tau+n}
        R_win = R_buf.T                                     # R_{tau+1} .. R_{tau+n}, (n, n_runs)

        G, weight = n_step_return(env, kind, n, Q, S_win, A_win, R_win,
                                  eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma)
        s_tau, a_tau = S_win[0], A_win[0]
        updates = not_terminal[s_tau]   # 0 while the window is still filling, and past T
        Q = pt.inc_subtensor(Q[runs, s_tau, a_tau],
                             alpha * updates * weight * (G - Q[runs, s_tau, a_tau]))

        return (rng, s_next, a_next, live * not_terminal[s_next], S_buf, A_buf, R_buf, Q,
                reward_sum + live * r, step_count + live)

    def episode(rng, s, a, Q, alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma, max_steps):
        """Run one episode in every run, then draw the next episode's start state and action.

        Parameters
        ----------
        rng : RandomGeneratorSharedVariable
            The random generator state.
        s, a : TensorVariable of int, shape (n_runs,)
            Each run's start state and first action.
        Q : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs, n_states, n_actions)
            Action values at the start of the episode.
        alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma : TensorVariable, shape (n_runs,)
            Each run's settings.
        gamma : TensorVariable, scalar
            Discount factor.
        max_steps : TensorVariable of int, scalar
            Steps per episode.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple
            ``(rng, s_new, a_new, Q, reward_sum, step_count, done)``: the next episode's start
            state and first action, the action values after this episode, and this episode's
            sum of rewards, number of steps and done flag, each of shape (n_runs,).
        """
        zero = pt.zeros_like(not_terminal[s])
        n_runs = Q.shape[0]
        pad = pt.zeros((n_runs, n), dtype="int64")

        (rng_final, S_seq, A_seq, live_seq, _, _, _, Q_seq,
         reward_sum, step_count) = pytensor.scan(
            fn=inner,
            outputs_info=[
                rng,
                s,
                a,
                zero + 1.0,
                pad + pad_state,
                pad,
                pt.zeros((n_runs, n)),
                Q,
                zero,
                zero
            ],
            non_sequences=[alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma],
            n_steps=max_steps,
            return_updates=False
        )

        Q_new = Q_seq[-1]
        rng, s_new = rng_final.categorical(p=pt.ones((n_runs, 1)) * start_dist[None, :])
        rng, a_new = pick(rng, Q_new, s_new, eps_behavior)
        return rng, s_new, a_new, Q_new, reward_sum[-1], step_count[-1], 1.0 - live_seq[-1]

    rng_a, s_first = rng_shared.categorical(p=pt.ones((Q_init.shape[0], 1)) * start_dist[None, :])
    rng_b, a_first = pick(rng_a, Q_init, s_first, eps_behavior)

    rng_final, S_out, A_out, Q_out, reward_sum, step_count, done = pytensor.scan(
        fn=episode,
        outputs_info=[rng_b, s_first, a_first, Q_init, None, None, None],
        non_sequences=[alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma, max_steps],
        n_steps=n_episodes,
        return_updates=False
    )

    return pytensor.function(
        [Q_init, alpha, eps_behavior, eps_target, sigma, gamma, n_episodes, max_steps],
        [Q_out[-1], reward_sum, step_count, done],
        updates={rng_shared: rng_final}, on_unused_input="ignore")

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
What one episode changes
Using the open room environment we show a similar idea as the Random Walk example, where the one-step Sarsa can only update one action value compared to ten action values with 10-step Sarsa
To draw the path next to the values it changed we run this one episode outside the compiled loop, under a uniform random policy, and write the book’s pseudocode out literally.






Note



The open room example below is still not control. It is Policy Evaluation only.



rollout_room = make_rollout(room, 61)
pi_uniform_room = np.ones((room.n_states, room.n_actions)) / room.n_actions
MAX_STEPS_ROOM = 400
ALPHA_ROOM = 0.5

S_room, A_room, R_room, S_next_room = rollout_room(
    pi_uniform_room,
    np.full(200, int(np.argmax(room.start)), dtype="int64"), # Starting states for each 200 episodes
    MAX_STEPS_ROOM
)

lengths = (~room.terminal[S_room]).sum(axis=0)
finished = np.flatnonzero(room.terminal[S_next_room[-1]])
chosen = finished[np.argmin(np.abs(lengths[finished] - 45))]   # a middling-length wander
T_room = int(lengths[chosen])

path_S = S_room[:T_room, chosen]
path_A = A_room[:T_room, chosen]
path_R = R_room[:T_room, chosen]

def n_step_sarsa_one_episode(n, alpha=ALPHA_ROOM, gamma=GAMMA_ROOM):
    """Run Sutton & Barto's n-step Sarsa update over the one recorded room episode.

    Policy evaluation only: the actions are the recorded ones (``path_S``, ``path_A``,
    ``path_R``), not chosen from Q. Starting from Q = 0, for tau = 0 .. T - 1,

        G = sum_{k=tau}^{min(tau+n, T)-1} gamma^(k-tau) R_{k+1}  +  gamma^n Q(S_{tau+n}, A_{tau+n}) if tau + n < T,
        Q(S_tau, A_tau) <- Q(S_tau, A_tau) + alpha [ G - Q(S_tau, A_tau) ].

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        Number of steps in the return.
    alpha : float, default ALPHA_ROOM
        Step size.
    gamma : float, default GAMMA_ROOM
        Discount factor.

    Returns
    -------
    ndarray, shape (n_states, n_actions)
        The action values after the episode. Only the pairs whose return reached the goal's
        +1 are non-zero.
    """
    Q = np.zeros((room.n_states, room.n_actions))
    for tau in range(T_room):
        horizon = min(tau + n, T_room)
        G = sum(gamma ** (k - tau) * path_R[k] for k in range(tau, horizon))
        if tau + n < T_room: # bootstrap only if the horizon is inside the episode
            G += gamma ** n * Q[path_S[tau + n], path_A[tau + n]]
        Q[path_S[tau], path_A[tau]] += alpha * (G - Q[path_S[tau], path_A[tau]])
    return Q

Q_room = {n: n_step_sarsa_one_episode(n) for n in (1, 10)}


goal_room = int(np.argmax(room.terminal))
start_room = int(np.argmax(room.start))
fills_room = [GRID_TERMINAL if s == goal_room else GRID_LIGHT.floor for s in range(room.n_states)]
path_xy = np.array([grid_xy(s, room.shape) for s in list(path_S) + [goal_room]])

room_fig = grid_panels(
    [f"{n}-step Sarsa: {int((Q > 1e-12).sum())} action values updated" for n, Q in Q_room.items()],
    room.shape,
    title="<b>Updates in one episode</b><br><sup>Orange arrows show updated action values</sup>",
    cell_px=45,
    theme=GRID_LIGHT
)

for col, (n, Q) in enumerate(Q_room.items(), start=1):
    draw_cells(room_fig, room, fills_room, {start_room: "S", goal_room: "G"}, row=1, col=col)

    room_fig.add_scatter(
        x=path_xy[:, 0],
        y=path_xy[:, 1],
        mode="lines",
        line=dict(color=colors[0], width=2),
        opacity=0.9,
        name="the path taken",
        showlegend=(col == 1),
        hoverinfo="skip",
        row=1, col=col
    )

    for s, a in np.argwhere(Q > 1e-12): # one arrow per updated pair: a cell crossed twice gets two
        x, y = grid_xy(s, room.shape)
        dx, dy = STEP[int(a)]
        room_fig.add_annotation(
            x=x + 0.42 * dx,
            y=y + 0.42 * dy,
            ax=x - 0.10 * dx,
            ay=y - 0.10 * dy,
            xref=f"x{col if col > 1 else ''}",
            yref=f"y{col if col > 1 else ''}",
            axref=f"x{col if col > 1 else ''}",
            ayref=f"y{col if col > 1 else ''}",
            showarrow=True,
            arrowhead=2,
            arrowsize=1.1,
            arrowwidth=2.6,
            arrowcolor=GRID_ARROW
        )

room_fig.update_layout( # grid_panels hides legends; this one names the path, below the grids
    showlegend=True,
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="top", y=-0.02, x=0),
    height=room_fig.layout.height + 30,
    margin_b=40
)

room_fig.show(config=dict(displayModeBar=False))

                            
                                            



goal_room = int(np.argmax(room.terminal))
start_room = int(np.argmax(room.start))
fills_room = [GRID_TERMINAL if s == goal_room else GRID_DARK.floor for s in range(room.n_states)]
path_xy = np.array([grid_xy(s, room.shape) for s in list(path_S) + [goal_room]])

room_fig = grid_panels(
    [f"{n}-step Sarsa: {int((Q > 1e-12).sum())} action values updated" for n, Q in Q_room.items()],
    room.shape,
    title="<b>Updates in one episode</b><br><sup>Orange arrows show updated action values</sup>",
    cell_px=45,
    theme=GRID_DARK
)

for col, (n, Q) in enumerate(Q_room.items(), start=1):
    draw_cells(room_fig, room, fills_room, {start_room: "S", goal_room: "G"}, row=1, col=col)

    room_fig.add_scatter(
        x=path_xy[:, 0],
        y=path_xy[:, 1],
        mode="lines",
        line=dict(color=colors[0], width=2),
        opacity=0.9,
        name="the path taken",
        showlegend=(col == 1),
        hoverinfo="skip",
        row=1, col=col
    )

    for s, a in np.argwhere(Q > 1e-12): # one arrow per updated pair: a cell crossed twice gets two
        x, y = grid_xy(s, room.shape)
        dx, dy = STEP[int(a)]
        room_fig.add_annotation(
            x=x + 0.42 * dx,
            y=y + 0.42 * dy,
            ax=x - 0.10 * dx,
            ay=y - 0.10 * dy,
            xref=f"x{col if col > 1 else ''}",
            yref=f"y{col if col > 1 else ''}",
            axref=f"x{col if col > 1 else ''}",
            ayref=f"y{col if col > 1 else ''}",
            showarrow=True,
            arrowhead=2,
            arrowsize=1.1,
            arrowwidth=2.6,
            arrowcolor=GRID_ARROW
        )

room_fig.update_layout( # grid_panels hides legends; this one names the path, below the grids
    showlegend=True,
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="top", y=-0.02, x=0),
    height=room_fig.layout.height + 30,
    margin_b=40
)

room_fig.show(config=dict(displayModeBar=False))

                            
                                            


Notice how the learner doubles back on itself in 10-step Sarsa, so the ten strengthened pairs sit in nine distinct cells, and the cell the path crossed twice has two of its actions updated.
Those ten values are now non-zero, so the next episode has something to bootstrap from as soon as it enters that neighborhood. Remember this doesn’t come for free, though. Those ten targets are the true return over ten sampled steps, and on a stochastic problem that is ten steps worth of noise.

title: N-step Bootstrapping
text:
Windy gridworld control
We sweep \(n\) and \(\alpha\) together and count the total time steps needed for 170 episodes. This allows us to measure of how fast the policy improves.

N_RUNS_WINDY, N_EPISODES_WINDY, MAX_STEPS_WINDY = 30, 170, 1200
alphas_windy = np.round(np.arange(0.1, 0.91, 0.1), 2)
n_values_windy = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]

n_learners_windy = N_RUNS_WINDY * len(alphas_windy)
repeat_windy = lambda x: np.full(n_learners_windy, float(x))
Q_init_windy = np.zeros((n_learners_windy, windy.n_states, windy.n_actions))
v_star_windy, _ = exact(windy, GAMMA_WINDY)
start_windy = int(np.argmax(windy.start))

steps_windy = {}
for n in n_values_windy:
    learner = make_n_step_control(windy, "sarsa", n, n)
    Q, reward_sum, step_count, done = learner(
        Q_init_windy,
        np.repeat(alphas_windy, N_RUNS_WINDY),
        repeat_windy(0.1),
        repeat_windy(0.1),
        repeat_windy(1.0),
        GAMMA_WINDY,
        N_EPISODES_WINDY,
        MAX_STEPS_WINDY
    )
    steps_windy[n] = step_count.sum(axis=0).reshape(len(alphas_windy), N_RUNS_WINDY).mean(axis=1)


windy_fig = go.Figure()

for i, (n, curve) in enumerate(steps_windy.items()):
    windy_fig.add_scatter(
        x=alphas_windy,
        y=curve,
        mode="lines+markers",
        name=f"n={n}",
        line=dict(color=colors[i], width=2),
        marker=dict(size=7, line=dict(color="white", width=1)),
        hovertemplate="<b>%{y:.0f}</b> time steps"
    )

windy_fig.add_hline(
    y=-v_star_windy[start_windy] * N_EPISODES_WINDY,
    line=dict(color="grey", width=1, dash="dash"),
    annotation_text=f"optimal ({-v_star_windy[start_windy]:.0f} steps/episode, if you never explore)",
    annotation_position="bottom right"
)

windy_fig.update_layout(
    title="<b>n-step Sarsa on the windy gridworld</b>"
          f"<br><sup>time steps to complete {N_EPISODES_WINDY} episodes, "
          f"{N_RUNS_WINDY} runs per point, eps = 0.1</sup>",
    xaxis_title=r"$\alpha$",
    yaxis=dict(title="total time steps"),
    template="plotly_white",
    hovermode="x unified",
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.0, x=0),
    margin=dict(t=100, b=100)
)

windy_fig.show(config=dict(displayModeBar=False))

                            
                                            



windy_fig = go.Figure()

for i, (n, curve) in enumerate(steps_windy.items()):
    windy_fig.add_scatter(
        x=alphas_windy,
        y=curve,
        mode="lines+markers",
        name=f"n={n}",
        line=dict(color=colors[i], width=2),
        marker=dict(size=7, line=dict(color="white", width=1)),
        hovertemplate="<b>%{y:.0f}</b> time steps"
    )

windy_fig.add_hline(
    y=-v_star_windy[start_windy] * N_EPISODES_WINDY,
    line=dict(color="grey", width=1, dash="dash"),
    annotation_text=f"optimal ({-v_star_windy[start_windy]:.0f} steps/episode, if you never explore)",
    annotation_position="bottom right"
)

windy_fig.update_layout(
    title="<b>n-step Sarsa on the windy gridworld</b>"
          f"<br><sup>time steps to complete {N_EPISODES_WINDY} episodes, "
          f"{N_RUNS_WINDY} runs per point, eps = 0.1</sup>",
    xaxis_title=r"$\alpha$",
    yaxis=dict(title="total time steps"),
    template="plotly_dark",
    hovermode="x unified",
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.0, x=0),
    margin=dict(t=100, b=100)
)

windy_fig.show(config=dict(displayModeBar=False))

                            
                                            


Past \(n=4\), learning degrades badly because on the windy gridworld the early episodes are wandering randomly for hundreds of steps, and a long \(n\)-step return computed from a near-random trajectory is mostly noise about a policy that no longer exists by the time the update is applied.

title: Planning and Learning with Tabular Methods
text:
Utilities & Environment Setup
A hands-on companion to Chapter 8 of Sutton & Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction.
So far the book has given us two families of methods that look quite different:
This chapter brings the two together. Its main claim is that both families do the same thing. Each one estimates a value function by backing up values, using the values of the states that can come next to improve the value of the current one, and then acts on those values:
\[
\text{model} \longrightarrow \text{simulated experience} \xrightarrow{\text{backups}} \text{values} \longrightarrow \text{policy}
\]
The only difference is where the experience comes from. When it is real, collected by acting in the world, we call the process learning. When it is simulated, generated by a model, we call it planning. Any learning update becomes a planning method as soon as we feed it simulated experience, and nothing stops one agent from doing both at once.
We work through the following topics:
We finish with a summary and recap.
As in the previous chapters, every environment here is a finite MDP: a problem small enough that dynamic programming can compute its exact optimal values. We call that exact solution the oracle and use it as an answer key. Every learner and planner in this chapter is graded against it, so we always know how close a method got, not just whether its output looks reasonable.
This chapter bends one rule from the earlier chapters. There, learners were never allowed to look at the model. Here planners are allowed to use one - that is what planning means. But the model a planner gets is always one of two things: a model it learned from its own experience, or one we explicitly hand it. Either way, the grading still comes from the oracle.
